name: Tucson Custom Sheet Metal
old_description: Need a standard item in a hurry, call or email us about our stock inventory.
about:
Tucson Custom Sheet Metal operates from a shop in Tucson, Arizona. The company has served the Tucson area for over 30 years, establishing itself as a local source for sheet metal roofing components. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The shop produces both stock and custom sheet metal roofing products, including flashing, scuppers, vents, cooler jacks, caps, and pipe jacks. Core processes include cutting, bending, and soldering; scupper and jack joints are fully soldered for water-tight seals. The facility stocks material in gauges ranging from 28GA to 20GA, with 20GA representing the maximum thickness the equipment can cut and bend. Copper and other premium metals are available by special request.

Primary customers are roofing contractors and construction projects throughout the Tucson region. The company maintains a stock inventory of standard flashing, scuppers, and vents for immediate pickup or quick shipment, while also fabricating custom pieces for unique project requirements.

The business emphasizes durability, noting that its products are made to last with fully soldered, water-tight joints. It positions itself as a local supplier capable of fulfilling both standard orders from stock and custom fabrications with short lead times for the Tucson market.

name: Turn-Key Medical Inc
old_description: Over 40 Year history of providing diagnostic imaging services resulting in "The Best Clinical Results" for our customers.
about:
Turn-Key Medical is based in Meridian, Idaho, and has been providing diagnostic imaging services for over 40 years. The company became 100% employee-owned in 2019, joining a group of employee-owned organizations in the region. While the exact founding year and founders are not disclosed, the business began as a provider of imaging equipment and support services.

The company sells, installs, and services a range of medical imaging systems, including computed tomography (CT), X-ray, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), ultrasound, angiography/interventional, women's health, C-arms, fluoroscopy, enterprise imaging, molecular imaging, and mammography. It also supplies accessories and provides applications support. Turn-Key Medical maintains a local parts depot at its Meridian headquarters and has service specialists positioned across its territory to minimize response times for mission-critical equipment.

Turn-Key Medical serves hospitals, clinics, imaging centers, and vascular labs across radiology, cardiology, orthopedics, and women's health specialties. Its vendor partnerships include Canon Medical, Novarad, QT Ultrasound, Orthoscan, and Ziehm, allowing it to configure systems for specific clinical needs.

The company emphasizes its employee-ownership model, local parts availability, and strategically located service teams as differentiators that deliver high equipment uptime and rapid support. Customer testimonials highlight after-hours dedication and quick turnaround on critical repairs.

name: Tuscarora Mills Showroom
old_description: High-quality American-made linen, organic cotton, and hemp fabrics from Tuscarora Mills.
about:
Tuscarora Mills operates from Bedford, Pennsylvania, where founders Dave and Heidi have built a weaving operation focused on natural fibers. The company’s origins are tied to a mission to revive domestic textile production using plant- and animal-based fibers, though a specific founding year is not disclosed.

The mill produces fabrics from hemp, flax (linen), organic cotton, Supima cotton, wool, mohair, and silk, often weaving on vintage looms. It sources raw materials from a network of domestic growers, processors, spinners, dyers, and finishers, aiming to keep the supply chain within the United States. Specific facility size, headcount, or annual volume are not disclosed.

The fabrics serve the apparel, home goods, and industrial markets, targeting makers, designers, and manufacturers seeking American-made alternatives to synthetic textiles.

The company positions itself as an alternative to oil-based synthetic materials and carbon-intensive global supply chains, emphasizing regenerative, biodegradable fibers and a commitment to local economies and artisan skills.

name: Two Sisters Mill & Mercantile
old_description: Weather and/or other issues (i.e. the sheep getting out) may arise that may determine opening and closing the shop.
about:
Two Sisters Mill & Mercantile operates in Jeffersonville, Vermont, at The Granary on Route 15. The business was founded by sisters Monica Case and Tamra Higgins, who trace their Vermont ancestry to Revolutionary War veterans Josiah Pond and a Sheldon settler. Tamra’s purchase of twin Shetland sheep over a decade ago sparked the venture into fiber, while Monica brought 34 years of healthcare administration and occupational therapy experience. The shop reflects a family-owned, small-business ethos rooted in the region’s agricultural heritage.

The shop functions as a retail mercantile and community hub, stocking yarn, raw fiber, and Schacht spinning and weaving equipment—both in-store and by special order. Inventory rotates through goods from more than 60 consignors, and the sisters host free weekly fiber hours and monthly spinning sessions. No manufacturing occurs on site; the operation centers on curation, education, and direct sales.

Customers include hand-spinners, knitters, crocheters, felters, and fiber tourists visiting the area. The shop serves local artisans seeking supplies and a venue for their work, as well as travelers drawn by Vermont’s fiber trail. Tamra’s own flock of Shetland and Shetland/Finn sheep supplies some of the raw material sold in the store.

The founders frame the business as a way to honor the alchemy of turning land and animal fiber into crafted goods, aiming to build a fair, sustainable marketplace for livestock raisers and fiber artists. This mission drives their emphasis on in-person shopping, consignment partnerships, and community events such as a planned 2027 fiber tour of Scotland.

name: U.S. Outdoor Lighting (formerly US Pole Co.)
old_description: LED outdoor luminaires, light poles, and architectural fixtures
about:
U.S. Outdoor Lighting operates from a modern facility in Palmdale, California, where it relocated in 2002 after originating in nearby Sun Valley. The company was founded in 1984 by Joseph Straus as U.S. Pole Co., Inc., and has spent more than four decades building a domestic manufacturing operation focused on architectural outdoor luminaires and decorative poles.

The company designs and produces LED outdoor luminaires, light poles, and architectural fixtures across six distinct product lines. Sun Valley Ltg covers traditional and historic designs; U.S. Architectural Ltg addresses contemporary site and area lighting with advanced optics; Amerilume Ltg supplies budget-friendly commercial and industrial fixtures; Ameriscape Ltg provides landscape lighting; U.S. Sport Ltg serves sports fields and courts; and U.S. Pole delivers poles, arms, bases, and accessories. Manufacturing is vertically integrated and performed in the United States, with products built to meet Buy American Act and Build America, Buy America (BABA) requirements.

Customers span architectural, commercial, industrial, sports, and landscape lighting markets. The fixtures are specified for projects ranging from gas stations, retail centers, and parking garages to city parks, school athletic fields, and dedicated pickleball or tennis courts. The company positions itself as a go-to source for professional outdoor lighting projects that require domestically manufactured, specification-grade products.

Compliance with Buy American Act and BABA standards is highlighted as a core differentiator for public-sector and infrastructure work.

name: US Foods CHEF'STORE
old_description: Since 1955, We've Been Changing With the Times to Better Serve You
about:
US Foods CHEF'STORE operates a wholesale cash-and-carry location in Columbia, South Carolina. The business traces its roots to 1955, and in March 2020 the former Smart Foodservice chain was acquired by US Foods and rebranded as CHEF'STORE.

The store stocks thousands of foodservice items — fresh and frozen meats, seafood, dairy, bakery goods, dry and canned groceries, beverages, packaging, and cleaning supplies — in a warehouse-style layout with wide aisles. No membership is required; any business or individual can purchase at wholesale prices. The location operates seven days a week, with hours from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Saturday and 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Sunday.

Primary customers are independent restaurants, caterers, and other foodservice operators in the Columbia metro area, including neighborhoods such as Five Points, Forest Acres, and Fort Jackson. The store also serves retail shoppers looking for bulk quantities. The company emphasizes a 60-plus-year commitment to customer service and product quality.

CHEF'STORE differentiates itself by eliminating membership fees, offering a broad assortment under one roof, and leveraging US Foods' supply chain for competitive pricing. The cash-and-carry model allows immediate pickup without delivery minimums.

name: US LED, Ltd.
old_description: US LED is a Katy, Texas-headquartered manufacturer of commercial and industrial LED lighting fixtures and controls, assembled in-house since 2001
about:
US LED, Ltd. is a manufacturer of commercial and industrial LED lighting fixtures and controls headquartered in Katy, Texas, a suburb of Houston. The company was founded in 2001 by Ron Farmer, who serves as CEO, and initially focused on LED sign lighting before expanding into general illumination in 2009.

The company designs, engineers, and assembles its products in-house at its Katy facility, employing between 51 and 200 people. Its portfolio includes indoor and outdoor fixtures, LED lamps, refrigeration and emergency exit lighting, sports lighting, sign cabinet and channel letter lighting, track lighting, power supplies, and lighting controls. US LED also provides lighting audits, photometric layouts, project management, turnkey installation, rebate management, and ROI analysis, and has completed more than 50,000 projects nationwide.

US LED serves a broad range of commercial and industrial sectors, including retail, hospitality, education, municipal and infrastructure, office and corporate campuses, self‑storage, sports venues, warehouses, auto dealerships, and convenience stores. Its customers range from Fortune 500 companies to regional businesses undertaking national multi‑site rollouts.

The company emphasizes ultra‑long‑life LED products rated up to 200,000 hours (L70), backed by a ten‑year warranty, and positions itself as a direct manufacturer that eliminates distribution markups. Its differentiators include on‑site engineering and 100 % testing, a nationwide network of certified installers for turnkey projects, and operational‑efficiency services such as HVAC optimization, energy management systems, and demand‑response programs.
